name: Dirty Yellow
lede: Dirty Yellow is a dense, greenish yellow named by the 2010 xkcd color survey, and one of the rarest colors we can match in painting.

sections.title: A survey name for a vivid, murky yellow
sections.body:
The only recorded source for Dirty Yellow is the xkcd survey of 2010, following the plain modifier grammar *dirty* plus [[yellow]] [1]. At hex #CDC50A it measures lightness 78 and chroma 79 in LCH, close in strength to the nearest ISCC-NBS block, a vivid greenish yellow only 1.1 units off, despite the word *dirty* in its name [1].

Its closest named neighbor is [[puke-yellow|Puke Yellow]], 2.3 units away and almost the same color, another xkcd name from the same 2010 survey [2]. Further out sit [[piss-yellow|Piss Yellow]], 4.1 units off and lighter, and [[citrine|Citrine]], 4.4 units off and lighter still [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this yellow in only 2 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, making it one of the rarest matches in the whole set [3]. Both are from Asian art: an 1700 Pahari court scene of King Bali and a Bonnard interior of 1891, a combination too thin to support any claim about era or region [3]. These are screen matches on photographs of varnished paintings, not a record of any pigment, and a count this small is closer to noise than to a pattern [3].

origin.named_after: a modifier of yellow: dirty + yellow
